There was a hypodense lesion in the renal pelvis, extending to the proximal ureter that was not filled with contrast measuring 5.03 × 5.36 × 5.98 cm (Fig. 2).

report.source_text: He was advised to undergo a nephrostomy for ureteral dilation followed by double J stent placement. A percutaneous approach for cyst removal was deemed very difficult in this patient, thus nephrostomy was conducted using an 8-8.9 Fr nephroscope. To be able to remove the cyst, the cyst wall had to be very thin and well-visualized to avoid renal parenchyma injury. However, in our case, the cyst wall was too thick and poorly visualized, thus cyst removal was not conducted. Cyst removal failed, thus we proceeded to perform ureteral dilatation. The double J stent was inserted and bleeding was checked. Four months after surgery, the cyst remained, but the patient was asymptomatic.

clinician.trajectory_summary: 27-year-old male presented with intermittent loin pain and 3-year history of partial urinary retention. Initial ultrasound showed pelvicalyceal dilatation and proximal ureteral dilation indicating PUJO but could not reveal cause. CT scan demonstrated a hypodense lesion in renal pelvis extending to proximal ureter causing grade III hydronephrosis. Imaging confirmed the lesion pressed the renal pelvic system and proximal ureter causing obstruction. No biopsy or cyst fluid analysis was reported to definitively confirm PPC. The patient underwent nephrostomy and ureteral dilatation with double J stent insertion after failed cyst removal due to thick cyst wall. Four months post-surgery, cyst remained but patient was asymptomatic.
